# Schema non-empty constraint audit

**Audit baseline:** `main` at `f3ddeb76` (2026-11-22). Scope: every direct-child `*.json` in `08-bmcp-protocol/schemas/`; **32** files were present.

## Summary

- Schemas inspected: **32** — the 2 files audited at `88bf4875`, plus the 30 merged by `#500`.
- Constraints inventoried: **5599** declarations over **5506** distinct `(schema, pointer, constraint)` triples in the 30 new files, plus the 93 already registered.
- Rulings: **29** field-class rulings, covering **223** distinct `(field, constraint)` pairs, projected onto all 5506 triples. Every row below resolves to one of them; no row is a template default.
- `minLength`: 4289 declarations — 4287 `minLength: 1`, and 2 `minLength: 3` (the PostgreSQL `X/Y` LSN floor).
- `pattern`: 1236 declarations across 9 distinct patterns; 1193 of them are the fixed-width `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` digest.
- Structural: 56 `minItems` (28 at 3, 18 at 1, 10 at 0) and 18 `minProperties: 1`.
- Verdicts in the 30 new files: **5492** rows "No — not legally empty", **14** rows "Yes — legally empty" (10 `minItems: 0` rows — `owner_admission_bindings` ×9 and `recovery_observations` ×1 — and 4 `request_highwaters`/`admission_highwaters` floors that 1.0.2 replaces with a conditional branch).
- Dispositions in the 30 new files: `Retain` for the rest; `Retain, conditional` (17), `Retain; narrowed in 1.0.2` (4), `Retain; superseded by 1.0.1` (1).

## How to read this table

Sections A is the original `88bf4875` audit, kept verbatim. Sections B–G audit the 30 schemas merged by `#500`, grouped by protocol family. Each family section opens with a family-level ruling: the reading of the schemas that produces the per-row verdicts below. The rows are the projection of that ruling onto each `(schema, pointer, constraint)` triple — the ruling is the judgement, the projection is bookkeeping. Where a field's semantics differ from its family (a conditional branch, a superseded revision, an explicit empty allowance), the row carries its own ruling instead.

## Decision rule

A required property is not the same as a non-empty collection. Required array keys may contain `[]`. For highwaters, a positive observed count or COMPLETE_NON_EMPTY status is evidence that at least one item exists; zero-count PARTIAL/NOT_ENUMERATED/UNAVAILABLE/UNKNOWN states may have no reportable highwater and must not synthesize one. Identifiers, digests, counters, signatures and reasons cannot be empty when supplied.

## B. `bmcp.applied-ack-*` — 2 files, 14 constraints

Two JF10 prepare-acknowledgement schemas (`1.1.0-jf10-bridge`, `1.1.1-jf10-prepared-gid`). Every constrained leaf is either a PostgreSQL engine identity (cluster system identifier, database OID, prepare LSN, prepared GID, native XID) or an opaque protocol reference/digest. Ruling: no field has a legal empty state — an empty system identifier names no cluster, an empty LSN is not an LSN. All 14 constraints retained.

## C. `bmcp.coc-jf10-unified-*` — 18 files, 5309 constraints

Eighteen revisions of one envelope family (`1.2.0`–`1.2.17`). Each revision reuses the same `$defs` vocabulary; the constraint set only grows, and a leaf keeps its meaning across versions. Ruling: references identify a concrete protocol object or authority, digests are complete fixed-width commitments, counters/generations/positions are canonical typed tokens, a signature is authentication material, and a reason states a rationale — none may be empty. Three structural constraints carry their own rulings below: `owner_snapshots` (one snapshot per owner authority), `owner_release_refs` (three owner releases at epoch completion) and `owner_admission_bindings` (explicitly empty when no applicable admission exists).

## D. `bmcp.i-owner-snapshot-attestation-*` — 1 file, 28 constraints

A single owner-signed attestation of the frozen I snapshot: snapshot/gate/attestation references, ledger query proofs, high-waters, ledger and set roots, and the signature. Ruling follows the COC family: identities, digests, tokens and the signature are never legally empty. All 28 constraints retained.

## E. `bmcp.recovery-cutoff-*` — 6 files, 83 constraints

Six revisions of the two-phase cutoff message set (`1.0.0`–`1.0.5`). 1.0.0 uses one flat enumeration status; from 1.0.1 the owner snapshot splits request and admission enumeration and epoch completion requires three owner releases. Ruling: the `minItems: 1` arrays sit in `then` branches conditioned on COMPLETE_NON_EMPTY (the COMPLETE_EMPTY branch caps the same arrays at `maxItems: 0`), so they are not unconditional non-empty requirements; `owner_snapshot_refs`/`owner_snapshot_digests` are `minProperties: 1` but also `required: [I, D, C]`; `required_owner_release_refs` is `minItems: 1` in 1.0.0 and `minItems: 3` in 1.0.1+.

## G. `bmcp.storage-prepared-participant-proof-*` — 1 file, 14 constraints

A storage-side proof that a prepared participant resolves at a given XID: engine identities (LSN, database OID, system identifier, GID), a base64url signature, a SHA-256 digest and a purpose. Ruling: engine identities, the signature, the digest and the purpose are never legally empty; `recovery_observations` is `minItems: 0` and is explicitly allowed to be empty when the resolution produced no observation.

| schema | location | constraint | may be legally empty? | disposition | rationale |

| `bmcp.storage-prepared-participant-proof-1.0.0.schema.json` | `/$defs/sha256` | `pattern=^[a-f0-9]{64}$` | No — a digest is a fixed-width content commitment | Retain | The digest is a complete fixed-width lowercase hexadecimal value; empty or partial text is not a content commitment. |
| `bmcp.storage-prepared-participant-proof-1.0.0.schema.json` | `/$defs/signatureEnvelope/properties/purpose` | `minLength=1` | No — a purpose must state why the record exists | Retain | A purpose string states why the record exists; empty text states nothing and cannot be reviewed. |
| `bmcp.storage-prepared-participant-proof-1.0.0.schema.json` | `/$defs/signatureEnvelope/properties/signature` | `minLength=1` | No — an empty signature carries no authentication material | Retain | A signature must carry authentication material; empty text cannot authenticate a record. |
| `bmcp.storage-prepared-participant-proof-1.0.0.schema.json` | `/$defs/signatureEnvelope/properties/signature` | `pattern=^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` | No — the base64url character set excludes empty text | Retain | The signature is base64url-shaped and must be non-empty authentication material; the character-set pattern only rejects bytes that could not be a signature encoding. |
| `bmcp.storage-prepared-participant-proof-1.0.0.schema.json` | `/$defs/storageResolutionPayload/allOf/1/properties/recovery_observations` | `minItems=0` | Yes — empty when resolution produced no observation | Retain | A storage resolution that observed nothing has no recovery observation to report; `minItems: 0` states that, and any observation that is present is still constrained by its own item schema. |

## Pattern note

Nine distinct patterns appear, totalling 1236 declarations, and all nine are closed lexical forms that exclude the empty string on their own: the `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` digest (1193), the `^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$` counter (16), the `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]*$` reference (9), the `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$` property-name form (6), the `^[a-f0-9]{64}$` SHA-256 form (3), the `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` GID/signature form (3), the decimal engine identifiers `^[0-9]{1,20}$` and `^[0-9]{1,10}$` (4), and the `^[0-9A-F]+/[0-9A-F]+$` LSN form (2). The guard conservatively registers every pattern, so the table registers them all rather than only the ones a heuristic would call non-empty.

## Scope and limitations

The scan covers JSON Schema files directly in `schemas/`, not recursive subdirectories, schema fragments embedded in Markdown, runtime validators, or external contracts. The guard detects new or changed `minProperties`, `minItems`, `minLength`, and `pattern` declarations. It does not prove that a retained constraint is normatively justified; that requires human contract review. It does not decide semantic validity of empty arrays or infer business meaning beyond schema rules.

No schema and no validator script was modified to make this gate pass. Closure criterion 4 of GAP-09 (run the guard in CI and block merges) is **not** satisfied by this change: CI billing is suspended, so wiring a gate into a workflow that cannot execute would create an unobservable red state. That criterion remains open and is recorded in the work item.

## Open questions for Owner H

These are findings from reading the schemas for this audit. None of them was repaired here — repairing them would mean editing schemas, which is outside this change.

1. **`secondary_high_waters` key naming, `recovery-cutoff` 1.0.3–1.0.5.** `propertyNames` requires `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$`, while the sibling `allOf` branches require keys `receipt_issue`, `receipt_consume`, `producer_domain_inventory_epoch` (I), `producer_registration`, `work_item`, `attempt`, `barrier` (D), `reservation`, `provider_attempt` (C). All nine are snake_case and none matches the pattern. Under `owner_kind` I/D/C, 1.0.3–1.0.5 therefore have no satisfiable instance. 1.0.0–1.0.2 do not have the `allOf` branches, so they are unaffected. This needs a ruling: either the pattern was meant to be `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`, or the required keys were meant to be UpperCamelCase.
2. **`owner_snapshots` shape change, `coc-jf10-unified` 1.2.5.** 1.2.0–1.2.4 use a 3-element array; 1.2.5 changes the same property to a `required: [I, D, C]` object. Both are non-empty by construction, but a consumer that validates 1.2.4 and 1.2.5 with the same code path will see a type change.
